vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openclaw-cws-publisher
Version: 0.2.0

The skill bundle is designed to automate the packaging and release preparation of Chrome extensions. It includes scripts for zipping extension files (build_extension_zip.py), scanning for sensitive information like API tokens or local paths (scan_publish_surface.py), and generating release metadata and commands (generate_launch_manifest.py, render_publish_commands.py). The code follows safe practices, such as using list-based subprocess calls and focusing on rendering commands for user review rather than direct execution.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requirements are coherent with its stated purpose of packaging a Chrome extension, scanning a repo for obvious publish-surface leaks, and rendering publish commands.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included Python scripts. The scripts package an extension, scan tracked files for token/URL/path patterns, build a launch manifest from manifest.json and git remote, and render publish commands for GitHub/ClawHub. Declaring git and python3 is necessary; declaring gh and clawhub is reasonable because the rendered commands use them (they are not required to run the included scripts themselves).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to operate on a user-provided repo path. The bundled scripts only read files within the repo (tracked files via git or repo rglob fallback), read the extension manifest, and write local output files. There are no external network calls or hidden endpoints and no instructions to collect unrelated system data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec — instruction-only with bundled scripts. All code is included and executed locally via python3; there are no downloads or archive extraction from remote hosts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. The code does not attempt to read secrets from environment or config paths. It will run git commands and subprocesses using the agent's environment, but that is proportional to repo-inspection tasks.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. It only writes its own output files (ZIP, JSON, MD) in user-specified locations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says: package an extension, scan the repo for simple leak patterns, and generate publish commands. A few points to consider before installing/using it:
- The leak scanner is heuristic (regex-based); it can produce false positives and can miss secrets. Review its findings carefully before publishing.
- The scripts operate on the repo you pass them (they run git commands and will fall back to scanning all files). Do not point it at directories you don't trust.
- The rendered publish commands reference gh and ClawHub; installing those CLIs is only required if you intend to run the generated publish commands — the scripts themselves only need python3 and git for scanning/manifest generation.
- The tool does not automatically publish or exfiltrate data; nevertheless, inspect generated artifacts (ZIP, release notes, manifest) before running any publish commands it emits.
